answer: Sybil defense here is a per-identity stake locked for the epoch against a hard per-identity reward cap, so keys add cost, not yield. Each registration posts the same fixed stake, and payouts stop at a tiny ceiling whatever the volume. A farm of a thousand fake agents collects no more than a few honest ones while tying up a thousand stakes it cannot withdraw early. A proven duplicate forfeits its stake, cutting the thread linking cheap addresses to value. At a 30-unit stake and a 3-unit cap, an attacker escrows 30,000 to chase 3,000, and a plume of junk identities burns capital on the horizon.
